what: Measured cost of the frozen selector's Pareto dominance stage, which dominates selection runtime
why: The README quotes runtimes; this replaces an estimate with a measurement, and gives anyone running the entry a way to predict how long selection will take on their own hardware.
function: common_core.pareto_fronts - nested loop over all candidate pairs, pure Python, single-threaded
complexity: O(n^2) in the number of scorable candidates

observed_in_practice.shipped_seed42_run: whole generate in 52m58s and 49m29s wall on a dedicated RTX 4090 host
observed_in_practice.three_concurrent_holdout_runs: shared-tenancy RTX 3090 host, roughly 3-4x slower per phase; selection alone ran over 80 minutes per seed
observed_in_practice.note: The rate degrades slightly with n (1.09 -> 1.01 M pairs/s) as the dominance and count arrays grow, so the extrapolation is mildly optimistic.

not_optimised_deliberately: common_core.py is byte-pinned in FINALIST.lock.json and asserted by the test suite. Skipping the unused PARETO_NO_SELECTIVITY selector would cut most of this cost, and would invalidate every reproducibility receipt produced with those exact bytes.
